content.text:
The drawing shows a benzothiophene core with a carboxylic acid on the thiophene ring and a nitro group on the benzene ring.

**Thiophene ring.** Sulfur is at the bottom. It is bonded to C2, which carries the COOH group, and to C7a, the ring-fusion carbon at the lower left. C2 is double-bonded to C3 and C3 connects to C3a, the other fusion carbon.

**Benzene ring.** Going around from C3a: C4 (upper right, the CH next to the fusion carbon), C5 (top left, bearing the NO2), C6 (left), C7 (lower left), then C7a.

**Nitro position.** The NO2 is attached to the carbon adjacent to C4, which makes it C5. This gives 5-nitrobenzo[b]thiophene-2-carboxylic acid.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cc2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2s1
